A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScoreMatchingRiesz work, with retained methods and proofs traceable across reorganization. All pages and appendices support comparison. V2 has display defects, including a caption-only Figure 5 and overflowing Table 9, but the table's embedded numerical text remains recoverable.

before.justification: V1 presents methodological constructions, mathematical arguments, and a Bregman-objective proof in Appendix A, but no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulations in Section 9 and Appendix P, including a joint-training ablation, and financial time-series estimates in Appendix Q, Table 9, and Figures 6–8.

M1.justification: V1 already contains denoising and time-score estimators. V2 adds joint data/time-score training, ratio calibration and clipping, and a cross-fitted policy-path estimator using known pushforward maps. It also corrects the stated time-derivative procedure: v1 differentiates through bridge samples, whereas v2 explicitly holds the sampled input fixed.

E1.justification: V1 has no evaluated datasets or scenarios. V2 evaluates AME, APE, and policy paths using a three-dimensional Gaussian design, high-dimensional Gaussian and mixture designs, and stochastic treatment interventions. Appendix Q additionally analyzes monetary-policy shifts and equity returns using financial and macroeconomic data.

E2.justification: Riesz regression changes from cited methodology in v1 to an evaluated baseline in v2 Tables 2, 3, 6, and 7. Table 8 compares Time-SMR with and without joint training. Appendix Q describes a financial-data Riesz comparison, but its reported table and plotted results do not establish that comparison.

E3.justification: V2 introduces empirical protocols absent from v1: two-fold cross-fitting, common outcome-regression architectures, population Monte Carlo truths, and bias, MSE, and coverage metrics. Appendix Q adds monthly preprocessing, full-sample nuisance estimation without splitting, specified policy-shift grids, and horizons from one to twelve months.

E4.justification: V1 contains no empirical ablations or robustness analyses. V2 examines stability under high-dimensional sparse and multimodal dense designs, directly tests joint training in Appendix P.3, and compares estimated policy paths with their local linear approximation. These additions investigate component effects and failure behavior.

E5.justification: V2 introduces reporting across 200 simulation trials, empirical coverage of 95% intervals, and pointwise policy-path confidence bands. Appendix Q specifies Newey–West HAC standard errors and pointwise intervals without multiplicity adjustment. V1 contains no corresponding empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds all empirical results. Tables 2–3 report Data-SMR/Time-SMR/Riesz MSEs of 0.161/0.637/10.076 for AME and 0.486/1.117/74.918 for APE. Tables 6–8 add different performance tradeoffs and ablation outcomes; Appendix Q adds horizon-dependent financial estimates. These are newly reported results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal policy-path and pushforward constructions, conditional score-estimation rates, proofs, downstream error bounds, and smoothing-bias/DML conditions in Sections 7–8 and Appendices G–L. The earlier Bregman proof is retained in Appendix H. However, Theorem 6.1's endpoint sum conflicts with that signed proof, and Appendix E.2 reverses the control-ratio integration direction relative to v1.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes stabilization and unification of score-based representer estimation. V2 makes policy-path estimation, convergence guarantees, and the loss/link covariate-balancing perspective explicit contributions. Its conclusion additionally claims demonstrated policy-path estimation and distinguishes the empirical preference for Data-SMR from Time-SMR's broader applicability.

C2.justification: V2 substantially qualifies the AME–APE connection through known pushforward structure and discusses smoothing bias, overlap, and exponentiation errors. It interprets low-MSE but poorly covered estimates in Appendix P. Appendix Q explicitly treats financial findings as predictive associations and acknowledges that dependent, unsplit data fall outside the main i.i.d. theory.

D1.justification: V2 expands v1's generic sampling and denoising guidance with Algorithms 1–3, network-sharing options, joint-loss weights, training schedules, calibration, and quadrature instructions. Appendix Q specifies preprocessing and concrete network sizes, training budgets, noise ranges, and 64 integration steps. Reproducibility remains incomplete, including unspecified simulation sample sizes and financial sample dates.

R1.justification: The introduction and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning across semiparametric efficiency, covariate balancing, score matching, and policy/local-projection analysis. Added references include Hyvarinen, Vincent, Oko et al., and Jorda, supporting relationships and theoretical claims beyond v1's shorter DRE-centered discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around Data-SMR, Time-SMR, and policy paths. Existing ATE material moves to Appendix E, infinitesimal-classification discussion to Appendix M.1, and the Bregman proof to Appendix H. The reorganization is substantial beyond the addition of scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 introduces applicability and results tables, error boxplots, policy-path panels, and algorithm boxes absent from v1. These substantially change the presentation of the method and evidence. Some additions are defective: Figure 5 contains only a caption, and Table 9 extends beyond the page's right edge.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's unsupported empirical stability claims through comparisons that also reveal undercoverage and failure cases. It replaces the loose AME–APE connection with a defined policy-path construction and applicability conditions, while adding conditional theory and implementation guidance. These are substantial gains in evidence and precision. New formula inconsistencies in Theorem 6.1 and Appendix E.2, incomplete experimental specifications, and unfinished appendix displays temper the improvement but do not outweigh those gains.
